transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Helios Head of Platform), Ethan Morales (Helios Security Lead), Katrin Vogel (Helios Procurement Manager)

Summary:
Quick legal touchpoint to align MSA/DPA redlines, confirm SLA expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted, and surface procurement signoff path + pricing thresholds. SE to validate perf on dedicated node; Redwood to provide redline and SOC2 artifacts.

Topics covered:
- MSA/DPA redline items (data residency, breach notification, indemnity caps)
- SLA obligations / uptime language and remedies
- Pricing approval path and committed capacity options
- Onboarding checklist and required vendor docs (SSO, KMS, audit logs)

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Rao: Priya here.
[00:10] Ethan Morales: Ethan on security.
[00:12] Katrin Vogel: Katrin from procurement.
[00:14] Marcus Patel: Marcus, Redwood SE.
[00:16] Laura Chen: Great, so agenda is short, we want to get through the legal redlines and the onboarding path. Hope that works?
[00:22] Priya Rao: Yeah, that's perfect. We're trying to keep this on a hard timeline, finance wants approval by end of May.
[00:30] Laura Chen: Understood. We'll try to be decisive. Marcus, quick note on the dedicated node perf snapshot - status?
[00:36] Marcus Patel: We're spinning up a NVLink cluster mirror for a 48 hour run. The test harness will do typical query mix from Helios logs, but small note: we had to relax batch sizing because Helios workload has some short prompt heavy tail, so numbers may be optimistic for larger batch sizes.
[00:50] Ethan Morales: Sorry, can you repeat the batch sizing point? That's critical for our latency SLO.
[00:54] Marcus Patel: Yeah, so the snapshot uses a mix that favors single-shot queries; if you push heavy batching the latency tails move a bit. We'll include p50/p95/p99 so you can see distribution.
[01:08] Katrin Vogel: Good. On the contract side, we circulated a redline to Laura last week. There are three major items procurement will not accept: broad indemnity, data residency clause loose language, and the 180-day limit on claims.
[01:24] Laura Chen: Thanks Katrin. To be explicit, Redwood's standard MSA has an indemnity carve that we can narrow — are you asking for mutual limited indemnity or carveouts?
[01:34] Katrin Vogel: Mutual limited indemnity with carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct. Also interesting point: we need clarity on subprocessors in the DPA — Helena, our privacy counsel, asked who has access to logs and where they're stored.
[01:48] Priya Rao: And on residency: our core PHI is in EU region; we need guarantee that logs with sensitive identifiers won't transit into US without explicit consent and KMS keys must be customer-managed.
[02:00] Laura Chen: Right. Quick callout: Redwood Private can run in your VPC with customer-managed KMS, but there are additional setup SLA and lead time. For Hosted API we do encryption at rest on our KMS unless you require AWS/GCP BYOK — which we can support with Private.
[02:18] Ethan Morales: So for the PoC we want to validate functional integration on Hosted but require encryption with our KMS for anything with PHI. Is that feasible?
[02:27] Marcus Patel: Hosted can be set up with a customer KMS via our partner flow but that path is slower — 4-6 weeks typically. If the timeline is tight, a dedicated Private node in your account would be faster to certify, but that requires network peering and extra ops work.
[02:45] Priya Rao: Finance wants pricing scenarios: hosted consumption vs dedicated committed capacity. Katrin, can you speak to what signoff looks like on the finance side?
[02:54] Katrin Vogel: We need a price delta and clear capex vs opex guidance. For dedicated we need committed monthly spend thresholds and an early-termination clause for the first 12 months.
[03:06] Laura Chen: We can provide a three tier pricing sheet: pay-as-you-go hosted, 3-month reserved, 12-month reserved with volume discounts. We'll include early termination terms in the commercial attachment.
[03:16] Ethan Morales: One more on SLA: Helios requires 99.95% monthly uptime with credit schedule and a runbook for incident response and postmortem. Is that part of Redwood Dedicated SLA?
[03:27] Laura Chen: Our Dedicated SLA is typically 99.9% by default; 99.95% can be contracted for at a different pricing tier and with stricter runbook obligations. Also note, for Private deployments the SLA is dependent on the customer's infra but we provide software SLAs plus response targets.
[03:44] Priya Rao: That's a key negotiation point for us. If we go 99.95 we need quicker MTTx for failover and a defined rollback plan.
[03:52] Marcus Patel: On the failover side, we support model variant fallback to smaller quantized variants to preserve availability, that can be automated but you'd need to accept the quality/cost tradeoffs.
[04:05] Priya Rao: Can we get an operational runbook excerpt?
[04:07] Laura Chen: Yes, we'll send a sanitized runbook and the incident procedure.
[04:11] Katrin Vogel: For the DPA, our legal asked to see subprocessor list and access controls — specifically audit log retention policy and who can request deletion.
[04:20] Marcus Patel: Logs are retained per config; default is 90 days but can be extended. Deletion requests follow a formal process; in Private deployments retention is under your control. Hosted has stricter controls but you can request deletions as part of the DPA process.
[04:33] Ethan Morales: Are audit logs encrypted at rest with customer KMS?
[04:37] Laura Chen: On Hosted, we use Redwood KMS by default. For Private we can wire customer KMS. We should mark that as a must-have in the redline.
[04:46] Priya Rao: Ok, timeline check — finance wants approval by end of May. That leaves five business days. Can Redwood realistically return a redlined MSA+DPA that addresses these items in that timeframe?
[04:57] Laura Chen: We'll prioritize; I can commit to sending a redline by Monday the 25th, assuming no new major asks pop up.
[05:03] Katrin Vogel: Monday works if we get it early.
[05:07] Marcus Patel: Back to technical: for the perf snapshot we'll attach attachments with p50/p95/p99 and token throughput. Any special throughput constraints?
[05:16] Priya Rao: For our search and summarization flows, p95 must stay below 350ms for single-shot prompts. If the p99 is higher that's acceptable but we'd like mitigation strategies.
[05:26] Marcus Patel: Noted. We'll include mitigation: prefix caching, KV cache warmup, and suggested batching policies.
[05:33] Ethan Morales: About SOC2 and certs — do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO?
[05:37] Laura Chen: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001; we'll share the attestation and the compliance pack.
[05:44] Katrin Vogel: Also need evidence of penetration testing schedule and bug bounty.
[05:48] Laura Chen: We'll include the pentest summary and our bug-bounty program link.
[05:52] Priya Rao: On subprocessors — can you confirm if any third party model hubs are used, and if so, which ones?
[05:58] Marcus Patel: We onboard open models and some partner-hosted checkpoints; typically all code and binaries are validated. We'll provide the subprocessor list in the DPA appendix.
[06:08] Katrin Vogel: For procurement, the final signoff needs procurement, security, and platform. Procurement will sign after legal and finance approve commercial terms. Typical path: redline -> legal review -> procurement scoring -> finance signoff -> exec approval. We need CRM tickboxes for each.
[06:23] Laura Chen: Understood. We'll annotate each change with rationale to speed legal review.
[06:28] Priya Rao: One operational risk: data residency for training/learning — we need assurance that no customer data is used for model training without explicit opt-in.
[06:38] Laura Chen: Redwood does not train on customer data by default; we can add a clause to prohibit training unless explicitly agreed and scoped.
[06:45] Ethan Morales: Can we get a DPA clause that explicitly restricts learning and model updates?
[06:49] Laura Chen: Yes, we'll add that as a non-derivative clause.
[06:53] Katrin Vogel: A couple of nitty-gritty items: bank details for invoicing, PO flow, and tax forms. Finance needs an invoice sample and billing contact.
[07:03] Laura Chen: I'll include a billing contact and invoice template in the follow-up packet.
[07:07] Marcus Patel: Small technical question from me — for the dedicated node, what are the maintenance windows and patch cadence?
[07:13] Priya Rao: (to Marcus) We prefer maintenance windows outside business hours, but we need notifications 72 hours in advance.
[07:19] Marcus Patel: Redwood schedules kernel/driver maintenance monthly with a 72-hour notice; minor patches can be pushed more frequently but we can coordinate for your environment.
[07:29] Ethan Morales: Let's talk about SLA credits. We need a clear credit schedule and an escrow for model weights in case of vendor exit.
[07:38] Laura Chen: We can include a credit schedule in the commercial terms. Escrow for weights is negotiable — for Private we can arrange transfer of owned artifacts on contract termination.
[07:49] Katrin Vogel: On termination, we want data export in structured format and support for migration.
[07:54] Laura Chen: We provide data export and a migration playbook as part of offboarding for enterprise.
[07:59] Priya Rao: Good. Quick question: is there an option to run the inference runtime in our GCP project with Redwood control plane?
[08:05] Marcus Patel: That's the Private deployment pattern: control plane managed by Redwood, runtime in your cloud (customer-managed). That meets most governance controls while keeping operational overhead lower.
[08:16] Laura Chen: I'll note that as the recommended path for Helios if you need KMS and residency.
[08:21] Katrin Vogel: Regarding cost model — if we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity, will you include a clause that allows rollover credits for unused tokens?
[08:31] Laura Chen: We do offer committed spend rollover credits up to a limit; we'll surface the exact terms in the pricing sheet.
[08:36] Ethan Morales: For the PoC we'd like a short pilot with logging enabled and strict retention of 30 days. Is that doable?
[08:43] Marcus Patel: Yes, we can configure a pilot with 30-day retention and escalate to longer as you move to production. We'll capture the exact retention in the DPA appendix.
[08:51] Priya Rao: One last legal ask — we need Redwood to accept our standard data breach notification timeline of 48 hours.
[08:58] Laura Chen: Our default is 72 hours; accepting 48 hours will be an exception and may require contractual carveouts on liability. We'll flag that in the redline and discuss options.
[09:10] Katrin Vogel: If Redwood agrees to 48 hours, we will likely accept a narrower liability cap.
[09:15] Laura Chen: Noted. We'll propose language.
[09:18] (brief cross-talk)
[09:22] Laura Chen: Okay, to lock this down — commitments from Redwood: send redline MSA+DPA by 2026-05-25; provide SOC2 + pentest summary and subprocessor list; SE to deliver perf snapshot by 2026-05-27. Katrin to provide procurement checklist and signoff owner by 2026-05-24.
[09:40] Katrin Vogel: Yes, and finance will aim to return pricing threshold by 2026-05-22.
[09:46] Priya Rao: We'll also share a small prompt corpus for the SE snapshot by tomorrow.
[09:51] Marcus Patel: Great, that will help make the snapshot realistic.
[09:54] Laura Chen: Any other outstanding items?
[09:57] Ethan Morales: Nothing else from security.
[09:59] Priya Rao: No.
[10:01] Katrin Vogel: No.
[10:03] Laura Chen: Awesome. I'll follow up with the redline and the packet. Thanks everyone.
[10:09] (meeting ends)
